transcript.customer: Can you guarantee the curtains will match exactly in real life?

advice.text:
No, I can’t guarantee an exact match in real life. Wall paint and fabric reflect light differently, and a curtain’s colour can shift with daylight, evening lighting and the folds of the cloth.

The most reliable check is to compare a physical fabric sample against your wall in both daylight and your usual evening lighting. A deliberately tonal pairing can feel more harmonious than attempting an exact match, especially when the materials have different finishes.
alternatives: Choose a deliberately tonal pairing rather than an exact colour match.
nextSteps: Compare a physical fabric sample against the wall in daylight and your usual evening lighting before making a final decision.

transcript.customer: What should I look for when comparing samples?

advice.text:
Hold each sample vertically beside the wall, near the window, rather than flat on a table. Compare it in daylight and with your usual evening lights, checking whether it looks noticeably pinker, yellower, greener or greyer than the paint.

Also notice the weave and sheen: tilt or gently fold the sample to see how shadows change its appearance. Aim for a relationship you enjoy, not necessarily an identical colour. A sample helps judge colour and texture, but won’t fully show the effect of a whole curtain.
nextSteps: Compare samples vertically beside the wall in daylight and evening lighting.
Check undertones, weave and sheen before choosing.
